text: I keep coming across mathematics projects that bring knot theory to bear on physical field equations - studying how knots show up in the solution fields themselves, whether as knotted electromagnetic or magnetic field lines, knotted vortex lines and tubes in ideal fluid flows, or knotted nodal lines of quantum wavefunctions satisfying Maxwell's, Euler's or Schrodinger's equations. How do the projects working in this area differ in the physical systems and equations they focus on?
reference_answer: KNOTDYNAPP takes an electromagnetic and quantum-mechanical route: it proves that every knot type can occur as a stable closed field line of an electromagnetic field satisfying Maxwell's equations, constructs optical and quantum vortex knots as the knotted zeros of wavefunctions obeying Schrodinger and paraxial equations, and ties a knot's fiberedness to whether the magnetic field induced by a current through a knotted wire vanishes anywhere. GEOFLUIDS works instead in fluid mechanics and spectral theory, proving the Arnold-Moffatt conjecture on knotted vortex lines and Kelvin's conjecture on thin vortex tubes in Beltrami and steady Euler flows, and answering Berry's 2001 question by building Laplacian eigenfunctions whose nodal sets realize any knot type. FLUSPEC, a companion geometric-PDE program, targets smooth stationary solutions of the 3D Euler equations with chaotic trajectories confined in knotted vortex tubes of any topology, and studies vortex reconnection in the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. All three apply knot theory to solutions of physical field equations, but KNOTDYNAPP centres on electromagnetic field lines and quantum vortex knots whereas GEOFLUIDS and FLUSPEC centre on knotted vortex structures in incompressible fluid flows.
notes: Seeds: candidate cp2 vector-09 proposed KNOTDYNAPP(101023017)+BOPNIE(682537) via euroscivoc 'knot theory'. Reading BOPNIE(682537) shows it studies boundary value problems for nonlinear integrable PDEs; 'knot theory' appears once in a passing list of fields where integrable equations arise, and no knotted structure is studied - REJECTED as a euroscivoc false positive. KNOTDYNAPP is a genuine seed. Completeness sweep (non-embedding): run_sql objective LIKE '%knot%' returned the full 31-row universe; the only genuine knot-in-physical-field projects are KNOTDYNAPP(101023017), GEOFLUIDS(633152), FLUSPEC(862342); abstract-topology neighbours QuantGeomLangTFT(637618, TQFT knot invariants), LDTSing(101030083, algebraic/torus knots in 4-manifold surgery), MM-CAHF(893282, Heegaard Floer knot invariants), REFINV, OXTOP, GENERALIZED, ROGW all OUT (knots studied abstractly, no physical field); GOKNOT(796969, protein-backbone gordian knot via molecular dynamics) and MaCChines(787115, protein origami) OUT (discrete polymer, not a field-equation solution); euroscivoc 'knot theory' = {KNOTDYNAPP, BOPNIE}. Pooled adjudication (k=20, 37 candidates): IN KNOTDYNAPP (ranks L1/D1/H1/R1; EM field-line knots, quantum/optical vortex knots, fibered-knot vs induced magnetic field); IN GEOFLUIDS (L4/D2/H3/R2; knotted vortex lines/tubes in Beltrami/Euler flows, knotted nodal sets in QM); IN FLUSPEC (L2/D3/H2/R4; knotted vortex tubes of any topology in Euler flows, Gross-Pitaevskii vortex reconnection). text: Among graphene projects that include a Swedish participant, how do the ones tackling antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections make use of graphene?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%' AND o.country='SE'

reference_answer: Of the 18 graphene-classified projects with a Swedish participant, two attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria, and each puts graphene to a different use. PANG (Pathogen and Graphene) builds graphene-based antibacterial matrixes by chemically functionalising them with antibacterial peptides and molecules such as menthol, then exploits the photothermal properties of rGO in suspensions and transdermal patches - among them a flexible skin patch that treats subcutaneous wound infections under photothermal irradiation - to kill pathogens non-invasively, while also probing the effect of these structures on the immune system and their mechanism of action. PEST-BIN uses graphene on two fronts: infection diagnostic kits built as disposable 'plug-and-play' chips of graphene functionalised with receptors that capture bacterial-surface biomarkers, containing only carbon and biodegradable polymers and now produced by the spin-out LayerLogic AB; and antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles and hydrogel/polymer coatings, loaded with antibiotics so that the resulting nano-weapon physically penetrates bacterial biofilms and delivers the drug inside them. Both therefore rely on graphene as an intrinsically antibacterial, functionalisable surface, PANG for light-triggered killing on the skin and PEST-BIN for sensing plus biofilm eradication.

text: Across the Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that include at least one organisation based in Italy, what kinds of approaches for monitoring volcanoes and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

reference_answer: The eight qualifying projects converge on making volcanic unrest measurable and interpretable in near-real time, along three complementary lines. text: Among the SME Instrument phase 1 projects classified under viticulture, how do the ones that build on a producer's own naturally occurring organisms, rather than on bought-in standard cultures, put those organisms to work in making wine?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle = 'viticulture' AND p.fundingScheme = 'SME-1' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the 14 SME Instrument phase 1 projects tagged viticulture take this route, and both make the producer's own resident biology the source of a wine competitors cannot replicate. MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) treats a winery's own bio-imprint as a commercial asset: it genetically selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts of different strains, so a house can keep dependable, robust fermentation and still bottle singular wines, the firm's stated aim being to recover the old diversity of wines without giving up modern production technology. Eternum works from the vineyard outwards: Bodegas Langa, with 150 years of winemaking expertise, profiles the vineyard's own microbiology and uses that profile both to draw up a highly specific low-impact pest control plan and to pick the site's own fermentation yeasts, then matures the wine together with those yeasts in a purpose-designed container that mimics the shape of a maturation deposit, so nutrients the organisms yield keep enriching the wine inside the bottle. The shared move is to replace a bought-in standardised input with an on-site biological one, LEV2050 packaging it as a technology any winery can buy and Bodegas Langa applying it to its own estate's production.

text: What have EU-funded research projects learned about how the judges at the global courts that put individuals on trial for the gravest crimes of war and mass violence understand their own role in shaping the law through their rulings?
reference_answer: Two projects speak to this. INCRICO interviewed judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and found that they see their duties as going well beyond applying recognised rules of law: they also treat fact-finding, dispute settlement, law-making, case management and governance - and, to a lesser degree, protecting the interests and values of the international community - as part of their judicial function, and these self-understandings feed back into the Court's deliberations, the drafting of its judgments and its use of separate and dissenting opinions. EaRL asked the same question of the wider international criminal bench, combining a systematic reading of all 240 available judgements of international criminal and hybrid courts (the ICC, the ad hoc Tribunals for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) and Rwanda (ICTR), and the Special Court for Sierra Leone (SCSL)) with over 40 in-depth interviews with judges, civil-society staff and government representatives, and traced empirically how routine practices of legal interpretation come to produce new legal meaning. Taken together, the two projects describe a bench that regards developing the law as one of its own achievements, and both look outward as well - INCRICO at how the Court's judgments are received as authoritative, EaRL at how a wider interpretive community of government officials, NGOs and other international courts takes up those decisions.

text: How do the aims differ between projects that study the woodwork of ships that sank centuries ago - what does each team hope those old ship timbers can tell them?
reference_answer: Both projects read the wood of ships that went down centuries ago, but they ask opposite kinds of question of it. ModernShip Project works on the structural remains of 16th-century wrecks of Mediterranean build - Mortella (1527, France) and Santiago de Galicia (1597, Spain), alongside the already documented Lomellina and Calvi I - in order to draft, for the first time, a Mediterranean technical model of how such ships were put together and to set it against the better-known Atlantic one, so that the continuous exchanges and technological transfers between the two nautical spaces can be described. TIMBER treats ship timber instead as precisely dated evidence about a resource: tree-ring work on the Swedish warship Vasa, built in Stockholm in 1628 and sunk on her first voyage in Stockholm Harbour, confirmed timbers from at least four distinct sources, including a Baltic and a west Swedish source, alongside purchase records naming eastern Sweden, Riga, Koenigsberg and Amsterdam, showing that even in heavily forested Sweden timber was imported from abroad. On the Boele Ship, a wreck dated to the 1380s found in the river Skienselva in southern Norway that sank with a cargo of whetstones from Eidsborg, every timber analysed - the keel included - came from the southern Baltic around the mouth of the Vistula River, which TIMBER reads not as evidence for the transport of timber but as a ship built at the Vistula mouth; both cases feed its account of the maritime timber trade from c. AD 1100 to 1700, with felling dates and regions of origin. The difference is what the wood is evidence for: for ModernShip it is evidence of design and construction practice in two coexisting technical cultures, for TIMBER it is evidence of where trees were felled, who traded them and how timber moved.

text: Some EU projects build solar-fuel photoelectrodes out of carbon nitride rather than a metal-based semiconductor, so they have to work out how to make the material themselves. How do those projects differ in the routes they use to produce and deposit the carbon nitride layer?
reference_answer: MFreePEC works bottom-up from the molecule: it encodes the composition of a family of metal-free CNX materials (X = P, B or S) into supramolecular precursors, uses the stable intermediate melem to synthesise CN photoanodes in the 5-20 min range at higher temperatures, and gets the layer onto transparent conductive electrodes by electrophoretic deposition, ultrasonic spray of precursors, doctor-blading, dip-coating and added precursor vapour pressure during calcination - a porous carbon-nitride photoanode containing reduced graphene oxide and a nickel-iron oxyhydroxide oxidation co-catalyst held photocurrents exceeding 0.45 mA/cm2 at 1.23 V vs. NHE for more than 35 h. CALSOL instead pits two whole synthesis routes against each other for its carbon-based artificial leaf - the traditional thermal polycondensation route and a plasma polymerization route - and its headline result is negative about the traditional one: the product of thermal polycondensation of melamine is not graphitic carbon nitride but a defective melon structure that degraded considerably during photoelectrochemical experiments, with a flatband potential drifting from approx. -1.5 V vs. Ag/AgCl to -1.8 vs. Ag/AgCl across pH. The contrast is therefore between engineering precursor chemistry and deposition method to build a durable working photoanode (MFreePEC) and testing whether an established preparation route yields a usable carbon nitride photoelectrode material at all (CALSOL).

text: Several EU projects set out to turn software that writes music by itself into something they could sell. How did they differ in what that software was meant to do for its intended users?
reference_answer: I2C8 turned the Lrn2Cre8 FET project's machine-learning work into a digital audio workstation plug-in for chord sequence generation, pitched to electronic musicians, producers and DJs as a 'musical sketchpad'; it deliberately stays small - predominantly sequences of up to eight chords - because its stated aim is to 'inspire' for composing, not to deliver complete compositions. AIVA, an AI that trained itself on 30,000+ classical music pieces, went the other way and offered content creators finished royalty-free soundtracks 'in the matter of seconds, and at the touch of a button', transitioning from a service to an embeddable Music Engine plus an API that lets third-party developers create hundreds of hours of soundtrack music, and it validated commercial feasibility by testing users' response and willingness to pay for the Music Engine public beta released in the second half of 2019. CALMUSgaming, from the Icelandic SME ErkiTónlist and built on its CALMUS technology, targeted computer games instead: its report says the software generates new background music as the game evolves, with minimal contribution from the composer, saving up to 90% of the time devoted to music composition, and the funded work was a feasibility study covering technical scope, markets and competition, a patent search and a 5-year financial forecast. FlowMachines, a PoC of the ERC Flow-Machines project, treated musical style itself as the asset to sell and set out to build a style manipulation prototype for the music synchronization business - music composed to be synchronized to existing media such as advertisements, movie music or video games - but its report concludes that 'Direct commercial exploitation of AI technologies per se is no longer a profitable route', that the team shifted to producing, distributing and monetizing content by the music industry's 'traditional means', and that they convinced top executives of a major music label to create a dedicated label specialized in the production and dissemination of music composed with AI technologies; on the legal side it catalogued the copyright issues in a report but 'considered that it was not worth addressing the issues raised by each copyright type'.

text: Which EU-funded projects study how companies and business groups try to influence the policies and regulations that governments adopt?
reference_answer: EU-funded research on this question sits mostly in political economy, and it covers both who does the influencing and what it achieves. Several projects put firms at the centre of trade rule-making: PROSPER studies firms that 'mobilize politically across global trade networks and influence trade policymaking in the European Union' and reports that because 'particularly resourceful firms are able to carry their political demands to policymakers, interest representation might be skewed in their favor'; TRASC builds a firm-level dataset of lobbying on the ratification and content of free trade agreements and on antidumping measures; DIA reports that the effect of industry lobbying on international rule-making depends on whether industries across countries share common or conflicting interests. Other projects work on domestic policy: BUSWEL compares the policy positions and strategies of business interest groups in Denmark, Sweden, Germany, Austria and the United States and, as delivered, focused on three policy fields - corporate taxation, inheritance taxation and wage bargaining - finding that the responsiveness of governments to business demands depends on the policy at hand and on the types of firms represented; MILO models how polluting firms' incentives to join a lobby group shape a policy maker's choice of environmental policy instrument; BIZPOL maps corporate political activity, 'all non-market activities by companies when they engage with governments and policy-making more broadly to advance their interests'. The set reaches further sectors and periods: POWERSHIFTS finds that 'firms in centralised systems have actively opposed policies that facilitate increased decentralisation' and that 'incumbent generators wield significant influence over energy policy processes'; MIGPSC asks how private security actors and the defence industry shape European migration management policy; GRIP-ARM asks how business power shapes the design of industrial policies in resource-rich countries; EFTA DEVELOPMENT traces how non-state actors including business lobby groups shaped EFTA's policies and priorities between 1958 and 1992; EURECON studies the influence of non-state actors including commercial banks and big business on European economic decision-making; and ClimActiv and CORPORATOCRACY treat corporate lobbying and corporate political power as questions of democratic legitimacy rather than of measurement.

GOLD RULE (tightened this pass): IN iff the project's own research, as stated in its objective or its published report sections, examines efforts to influence public policy, regulation or rule-making AND the influencing actor is identified in the project's own text as business, firms, corporate or industry. OUT: the project's own advocacy or dissemination; passing background mentions; an influence claim attributed only to a cited literature rather than to the project's own findings; influencers named only as lobbies, special interests, interest groups or lobbyists with no business identification; and the reverse direction (regulation acting on an industry). text: What separation-management approaches for drone traffic have European U-space projects developed themselves - their own methods for keeping drones apart and resolving conflicts - as opposed to demonstrating separation services supplied by others?

pooling_evidence.note: single pooled run at k=40 over the final wording; 57 distinct pooled projects = 9 accepted-from-pool + 48 rejected. 776293 GAUSS is gold but retrieved by no condition at k=40; its provenance is the completeness sweep, recorded here rather than folded into the pooled arithmetic. hybrid_rerank returns 20 projects (reranker stage cap), the other three conditions 40.

reference_answer: European work on U-space separation splits between designing the separation service itself and validating deconfliction technology in flight. BUBBLES formulates a U-Space advanced (U3) separation management service at TRL3, computing UAS collision risk so that separation minima and methods - procedural, tactical self-separated or tactical ground-based - can be derived from a stated probability of collision. USEPE studies separation methods for demanding environments such as cities and applies machine learning to automate safe separation and deconfliction while holding airspace capacity. Metropolis 2 treats airspace design, flight planning and separation management as interdependent at high traffic density, comparing concepts that differ in how separation is performed (strategic/tactical, ground/air) by simulation before a real-world demonstration, while DACUS embeds separation management in a Demand and Capacity Balancing process and searches for the optimal balance between on-board separation intelligence and U-space separation service intelligence. LABYRINTH takes the centralised route, computing 4D paths for drone swarms so trajectories do not collide. On the technology and demonstration side, CLASS matured ground-based tracking with tactical deconfliction tools that suggest new conflict-free trajectories; IMPETUS tested tactical de-confliction in which virtual weights attached to each drone define the separation criteria, giving dynamic separation; TINDAiR demonstrated AI-based tactical deconfliction with a detect-and-avoid service over VTOL flights; GOF2.0 validated an architecture for highly automated real-time separation assurance in dense urban airspace; and GAUSS approaches coordination among UAS through Galileo-EGNOS precise positioning plus tactical deconfliction services in its UTM system.
notes: Membership criterion is now STATED IN THE QUESTION: a project is gold iff its own stored text shows it developed or validated its own method for keeping drones apart or resolving conflicts between them (separation minima, strategic or tactical deconfliction, conflict detection and resolution) within U-space/UTM; a project that only demonstrates or consumes a separation-type service supplied by partners is excluded by the question's own words ('as opposed to demonstrating separation services supplied by others'), as is on-board sensing hardware and manned-aviation separation work. The earlier 'large numbers of drones' qualifier was dropped because gold members TINDAiR (largest exercise: 'Deconfliction between an autonomous drone, an eVTOL carrying a passenger and a manned helicopter') and GAUSS ('4 UTM coordinated RPAS') do not satisfy it. text: Which projects are aimed specifically at preventing, or detecting at an early stage, the skin and tissue damage that long periods of unrelieved pressure inflict on bedridden or wheelchair-bound patients?
reference_answer: Six H2020 grants in this corpus are aimed at this problem, and most are sensing-plus-prevention systems rather than treatments. i-LiveRest (696939) and its successor grant LiveRest (830134) put impedance, pressure, temperature and humidity textile sensors on a wheelchair or mattress to score Tissue Viability in real time and then trigger the prevention strategy that suits the user and context; their target group is Spinal Cord Injury patients, 85% of whom develop such an injury. Qone (735302) does the equivalent for bedridden patients with a pressure-relieving mattress carrying temperature and pressure mapping sensors feeding a personalised risk-score algorithm, claiming roughly a 75% reduction in new cases. The two JUMPAIR grants (709595, 783594) build a smart anti-decubitus mattress system that remotely tracks known ulcer-activity biomarkers to raise early alerts to the hospital. STINTS (811965) is the research and training strand: it studies the biomechanical and biochemical pathways by which prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity, in order to improve preventative aids such as mattresses and insoles, early-stage diagnosis through non-invasive biomarkers and sensors, and ultrasound therapy.

text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to at least one named element, isotope or ion species. Naming a species is the test; the NUMBER of species is not - a project referencing one species and a project referencing two are both in, and the answer field carries the multiplicity. The test is also about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans, components and completed work are treated alike. text: A project set out to work out how often rivers across Spain and neighbouring parts of southwestern Europe burst their banks and caused serious damage, going back hundreds to thousands of years before gauge measurements began, by reading the bands of mud that had settled on lake bottoms. text: Which project brought historians of philosophy together with theoretical physicists to compare the conceptions of time in Plato and Kant with emergent time in quantum gravity and quantum cosmology?
reference_answer: PROTEUS (project 758145), 'Paradoxes and Metaphors of Time in Early Universe(s)'. It built a multi-disciplinary team of historians of philosophy, philosophers of physics and theoretical physicists to study how Western philosophy represents time in cosmology, examining the notions of time and the paradoxes arising in the philosophy and cosmology of Plato and Kant and setting them against the fundamental characters of emergent time in current quantum gravity and quantum cosmology. Its results include the digital archive 'Timaeus and Its Legacy', the COSMOS Network, and the edited volume 'Time and Timelessness in Fundamental Physics and Cosmology' (Springer 2024).

text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is to study working memory, how do the ones concerned with ageing investigate it in older adults?

reference_answer: Three of the 18 Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships whose stated aim is working memory are built around ageing, and each comes at it differently. Motivageing applies the Motivation-Cognition Interaction (MoCoInt) framework to healthy older adults and to Parkinson's disease patients, combining multimodal functional neuroimaging with a new working-memory training procedure and a randomised controlled drug trial aimed at raising working-memory capacity. COMEDM asks whether working memory and decision-making run on one shared neural circuit, using recurrent neural network modelling, EEG decoding and pupillometry, and carries the same paradigm over to older adults, where preliminary data indicate that degraded sensory encoding is a dominant source of age-related increase in WM and DM error.

text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects whose abstract mentions autism, which ones carry out their experiments in a non-human species, and which species do they use?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%autis%' OR p.title ILIKE '%autis%') AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Nine of the 29 ERC Starting Grants whose abstract mentions autism run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data. Rodents dominate: THERAUTISM screens molecular targets and a gene-therapy vector in preclinical mouse models of ASD, REVERSEAUTISM pairs Slc7a5 and BCKDK mutant mice with human cerebral organoids, DisConn images the awake mouse and maps the mouse axonal connectome, SafeFate characterises Myt1l knockout mice alongside human induced neurons, and NEUROGOAL and MotivatedBehaviors both record from circuits in behaving mice. Three step outside rodents - HomeoBalanceExcInh dissects excitation/inhibition balance in Drosophila Kenyon cells, MultiSense records whole-brain activity in larval zebrafish, and Brain2Bee tests its dopamine model in the honey bee.
notes: Filter: fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' plus the '%autis%' text condition over objective and title, which is what makes the survivor set enumerable (29 survivors). The question's anchor is worded to describe exactly what the filter reads - the project's own abstract - so a project whose only autism tie is in its published report (e.g. 637591 NEURAL AS, whose report mentions 'autistic spectrum disorders' while its abstract does not) is outside the question as well as outside the survivor set. At the runtime the structured half carries only fundingScheme; the topical half falls to retrieval (scoped.py whitelists no subject-matter column). Adjudication was exhaustive: all 29 survivor objectives read, plus workPerformed/finalResults for every IN and borderline case, plus a survivor-scoped SQL species sweep (mouse/mice, rat/rodent, zebrafish, Drosophila/flies, honey bee, monkey/macaque/primate/ferret/C. elegans over objective + report text). The adjudication test is whether the project's own text shows it carrying out experiments in a named non-human species. IN (9): 639489 HomeoBalanceExcInh - Drosophila Kenyon-cell circuit, 'allowing flies to learn to discriminate between different odours'; 677878 NEUROGOAL - two-photon imaging in 'foraging mice' and a mouse model of autism; 715508 REVERSEAUTISM - 'Employing a series of mouse models', plus human cerebral organoids; 715980 MultiSense - 'brain-wide response of larval zebrafish'; 757583 Brain2Bee - 'an animal model, the honey bee'; 802371 DisConn - 'recordings in the awake mouse', 'mouse axonal connectome'; 804710 SafeFate - 'new Myt1l knockout mouse models'; 851231 THERAUTISM - 'the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD'; 949652 MotivatedBehaviors - 'I characterized in mice a novel circuit', mouse models of psychiatric disease. OUT (20): 636458 CogSoCoAGE, 676943 SLAB, 678286 CONTEXTVISION, 678733 CAASD, 679927 SYNAPLAST MR, 715824 POINTS, 716974 Becoming Social, 755816 AUTISMS, 801708 ANTICIPATE, 801715 PUPILTRAITS, 804881 NEUROEPIGENETHICS, 852570 CoCoFlex, 852885 INDIVISUAL, 853211 DEVCOM, 946228 DEFEND, 948545 TrackingMinds, 950010 FamilySleeps - human participants, human cohorts, human imaging/gaze/pupillometry data, algorithms or ethics work, with no species keyword anywhere in objective or report text; plus three that do experimental biology without ever showing an experiment in a named species - 716011 NANOGLU ('synaptic proteins endogenously expressed in neurons'), 950013 CERCODE ('models of early cerebellar disruptions'), and 803984 GIDE, whose only species word in the whole record is the abstract's closing CV clause 'my extensive training in viral and mouse genetic techniques' while all four report sections (lineage barcoding, single-cell transcriptomics, membrane-potential perturbation) name no organism.
